relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a 13-year-old girl carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: "a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in TNFAIP3" (c.2199C>A, p.(Cys733*)), co-occurring with a RAD21 variant.
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcription (the only table is an abbreviation list). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5; 'the proband' is a role word). Previously published CdLS+psoriasis cases (Lubkov 2018, Mugheddu 2020, ref [17] Pakistan case) are out of scope: no TNFAIP3 variant or HA20 diagnosis described for them. RAD21 variant recorded as an other-gene variant unambiguously attributed to the patient. Inheritance 'not reported' for both variants: Figure 2 and 3 legends call them 'de novo', but no parental testing is described (rule 8). Functional evidence 'not reported': only in silico AlphaFold structural modelling, UniProt variant viewer and GEO knockdown expression data (not an assay of this variant). Contradictions in the paper: RAD21 classification given as 'likely pathogenic', 'probably pathogenic' and 'pathogenic for CdLS type 4'; RAD21 transcript printed as NM_006265.2 and NM_006265.1 (and NM_006265.3 in ref 53), and coordinates printed as chr8:10,673,499–10,658,686 and chromosome 8 position 116,852,561 (GRCh38); methods say GRCh37/hg19 while legends give GRCh38 positions; text says the TNFAIP3 and RAD21 variants change a 'Glycine' although the protein notation gives Cys733 and Gln436; a first skin biopsy was 'compatible with pemphigus foliaceus' before a later biopsy confirmed pustular psoriasis (pemphigus not recorded as a feature). The 'upper-limb reduction defects that range from subtle phalangeal abnormalities to oligodactyly' phrase in the physical examination repeats the Introduction's generic CdLS description and is absent from the Methods examination, so it is uncertain for this patient; recorded as stated. Neurocognitive features (dysprosody, limited social interaction) not mapped to the CNS-involvement checklist item. Growth failure checklist item set observed from 'short stature, low weight-for-age'. Age 13 years recorded as age at last evaluation; onset age not stated (only an 8-month history). No explicit absent findings, no treatment, no inflammatory markers reported.
